conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Split-Flap Board
style.description: A mechanical railway/airport departure board in a dim hall: rows of black split flaps with off-white characters in a dark powder-coated housing with a brushed-metal header, row lamps, and a warm raking key light; every character cycles forward through the alphabet to arrive.

brushed.description: horizontal brushed-metal streaks (fbm stretched along x)

motion: Characters never cut: each cell steps forward through the charset (blank, A-Z, 0-9, punctuation) one flap at a time, ~15 flips/s.
Cells in a row start ~0.034 s apart left to right with seeded jitter, so rows resolve as a ripple with different arrival times.
Each flap falls gravity-style about the centre axle (front = top of the old character, back = bottom of the new) and rebounds off the stop.
Lamps switch when a row's status settles; NOW BOARDING blinks green.
Camera: slow push-in with gentle lateral drift so the recessed slots and housing depth parallax; never cut.

objects.procedural: 44 x 26 m dark concrete hall wall 1.9 m behind the board

split-flap departure board: powder-coated housing, brushed header strip, 17-cell header, 6 rows x (14 + 12) cells, 15-cell footer, 3 lamps per row; each cell = static top/bottom halves + falling flap (instanced)

notes.mechanism: Each cell steps forward through the charset ' A-Z 0-9 - . : / & '' at ~15 flips/s; flip state is a pure function of t (flaps.cellState). The SCORE is generated from flaps.flipEvents of the same plan.
